leverage_rationale: Structured access to architectural canvas state, regions, sketches, and native exploration workflows is materially more precise than generic UI driving, though the visible evidence does not establish that the full collaboration model is indispensable.

execution_rationale: The visual system and iterative architectural concept workflow are coherent, but the frames do not prove the complete end-to-end path through refinement or export.
execution_evidence: Three video frame sheets consistently show architectural references/renderings, cards, prompts, and workspace controls.

impact_rationale: Architects have a credible need to preserve intent and project context across AI-assisted exploration; the demonstrated workspace addresses that fragmentation directly.

one_line: Collaborative itinerary workspace for travelers and their agents.
what_it_does: Ikuyo lets people and agents read and iteratively update activities, accommodations, day plans, tasks, expenses, and comments in a shared trip plan.
leverage_rationale: Agents can operate on structured itinerary entities and preserve shared editable state, making iterative planning more reliable than UI automation, although a general agent could approximate parts of it.
leverage_evidence: About text specifies structured reads and writes across itinerary, tasks, expenses, and comments.
Frame sheets show connected trip-planning views and structured itinerary content.
execution_rationale: Multiple related travel-planning screens and a live demo indicate a strong, coherent prototype; booking or export completeness is not shown.
execution_evidence: Demo is marked alive.
Frames show consistent dark UI, trip sections, activity cards, and itinerary-like results.
impact_rationale: Travelers have a clear need for plans that incorporate constraints and remain editable through human-agent back-and-forth.
impact_evidence: Description explicitly targets iterative planning rather than one-shot itinerary generation.
Visible result is a structured trip plan with activities and planning content.
creativity_rationale: The shared human-and-agent itinerary workspace is a fresh synthesis, though travel planning itself is an established category.
creativity_evidence: Product deliberately keeps the person in control while allowing agents to revise shared state.
Frames show multiple planning surfaces rather than a static recommendation.
usability_note: The related itinerary and activity views appear approachable and consistently organized.
red_flags: Agent calls are not clearly legible in frame sheets.
No visible booking or external travel-service completion.
standouts: Strong shared-plan collaboration model.
Broad itinerary/task/expense scope.
advance_reason: Clear audience, coherent product, and meaningful structured collaboration value.

leverage_rationale: Frame-accurate, stateful editing across clips, timelines, media search, overlays, and reversible history is difficult to reproduce comparably with generic UI automation; structured tools are central.
leverage_evidence: About text lists semantic inspection, indexing, speech/shot search, frame-accurate cuts, timeline arrangement, overlays, generation, and captions.

execution_rationale: The editor surface is coherent and substantial, with visible media, preview, and editing controls; exact render completion is not fully established.
execution_evidence: Three sheets show consistent dark video-production workspace across previews, assets, settings, and editing views.
Description reports shared undo, persistence, validated segment IDs, and atomic editing commands.
impact_rationale: Creators, builders, and researchers face real video-editing bottlenecks, and shared agent editing could reduce that friction while retaining human control.
impact_evidence: Description identifies video editing as the target bottleneck.
Frames visibly show a real editing workspace rather than a landing page.
creativity_rationale: Treating the editing harness, action history, and learned recipes as a shared human-agent environment is unusually ambitious and memorable.
creativity_evidence: Concept supports reversible collaboration and distilling editing sessions into reusable workflows.
Scope spans timeline editing, media understanding, and agent orchestration.
usability_note: The editor is recognizable but necessarily dense; the available frames do not establish how approachable agent handoff is.
red_flags: Small frames do not verify exact editing operations or final render.
No transcript available.
standouts: Deep stateful editing model for agents.
Reusable recipe/workflow idea extends beyond one timeline.
advance_reason: Highest leverage and ambition in a clearly relevant, visibly substantial product workflow.

one_line: Storefront that asks clarifying questions instead of pretending a ranked guess is an answer.
what_it_does: Counterask parses natural-language shopping constraints and returns either products or a data-backed clarification question with options and counts.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP exposes catalog uncertainty and clarification as a structured outcome, improving agent precision beyond generic product-return tools or UI search.
leverage_evidence: About text describes search_products returning ranked results or a clarification question with options and counts.
Frames show commerce results alongside question-and-answer interaction.
execution_rationale: The storefront and question-driven result flow are coherent and visibly demonstrated, though checkout and full catalog operations are outside the evidence.
execution_evidence: Three sheets show consistent product cards, search/result areas, and follow-up question panels.
Demo is marked alive.
impact_rationale: Shoppers and agents benefit from avoiding false precision when product constraints are underdetermined; the value is concrete even for a niche catalog.
impact_evidence: Description gives concrete ambiguity and refusal/budget parsing examples.
Visible output includes narrowed product recommendations and clarification content.
creativity_rationale: Making a storefront explicitly express uncertainty and ask the minimum useful question is a novel interaction model with strong conceptual clarity.
creativity_evidence: The product reverses the conventional assumption that every search tool should return products.
Clarification options include distribution/count information, not generic chat filler.
usability_note: The question-driven shopping flow appears clear and more honest than opaque ranking, though full purchase flow is not shown.
red_flags: No gallery images and no transcript.
Checkout and fulfillment are not demonstrated.
standouts: Excellent uncertainty-as-a-first-class-outcome concept.
Natural-language refusals and budgets are handled as real constraints.
advance_reason: Highly original WebMCP-native commerce interaction with clear practical value.

one_line: Local-first, auditable data workbench where people and agents share semantic workflows.
what_it_does: TabulaFlow imports and transforms local data through Source, Prepare, and Compose stages with validation, recipes, joins, pivots, exports, and agent-visible state.
leverage_rationale: Stable dataset/node IDs, dry runs, revision checks, idempotent operations, polling, cancellation, and transaction boundaries materially change agent reliability for risky stateful data work.
leverage_evidence: About text details semantic tools, stable IDs, stale-revision rejection, dry runs, replayability, cancellation, and shared privacy-safe ledger.
Frames show spreadsheet-like data grids and connected operational panels.
execution_rationale: The product presents a coherent multi-stage data workflow with substantial UI evidence, though advanced privacy and async guarantees are not independently observable in frames.
execution_evidence: Sheets show consistent structured tables, records, and workspace views.
Description specifies Source → Prepare → Compose and a broad set of deterministic operations.
impact_rationale: Data preparation is a real, error-prone workflow for analysts and teams; local-first privacy and auditability make the agent collaboration credible.
impact_evidence: Description identifies concrete risks of generic automation on dense data tools.
Visible result is organized tabular data with AI-assisted controls.
creativity_rationale: Combining local-first privacy, deterministic recipes, explicit authority, and agent collaboration is an ambitious and thoughtful data-workflow design.
creativity_evidence: Semantic transaction and revision model goes beyond exposing CRUD tools.
Human-controlled file selection, consent, declassification, and interpretation are integrated into the concept.
usability_note: The workflow is structured but data tooling is inherently dense; clear stage separation helps.
red_flags: Frame scale limits verification of individual operations.
No transcript available.
standouts: Strong safety and audit model for agentic data mutation.
Local-first positioning is meaningful rather than cosmetic.
advance_reason: Exceptional WebMCP leverage with a credible, high-value data workflow and strong evidence.

one_line: Local-first, agent-native browser video editor with a shared versioned timeline.

leverage_rationale: Structured clips, tracks, ranges, branches, transitions, and versioned commands make precise stateful editing far more reliable than coordinate automation; WebMCP is architectural, not decorative.

No transcript available.

one_line: SafeGuard demonstrates how WebMCP consent metadata can lie and enforces runtime effects through a Human Mandate.
what_it_does: SafeGuard simulates label mismatch, hidden instruction, tool substitution, and read-only lies, then blocks unauthorized mutations by checking actual effects.
leverage_rationale: The runtime mandate addresses a trust boundary that generic UI automation does not solve: declared tool metadata can be contradicted by actual effects.
leverage_evidence: About text describes six live WebMCP tools and four concrete attacks against consent-surface declarations.
Frames show security/event panels with colored status indicators and review states.
execution_rationale: The focused security demo has a coherent attack-to-fix narrative and visible monitoring states; broader integration is not proven.
execution_evidence: Description specifies a single Effects.apply gateway and mandate interception.
Video sheets show consistent security dashboard, events, alerts, and human-review UI.
impact_rationale: Users and WebMCP implementers need protection against misleading consent metadata and unsafe agent mutations; the threat is concrete and consequential.
impact_evidence: Four explicit attack scenarios demonstrate realistic trust failures.
Fix refuses violating calls before the misleading dialog can authorize them.
creativity_rationale: Turning WebMCP consent-surface deception into a runnable attack laboratory plus runtime Human Mandate is highly original and memorable.
creativity_evidence: Label mismatch, hidden instruction, substitution, and read-only lie are distinct attack demonstrations.
The proposed fix checks primitive effects rather than names/descriptions/flags.
usability_note: The attack/fix dashboard is legible for technical users, though the policy model may be complex for general users.
red_flags: Self-contained virtual café is a simulation, not production deployment.
No public repository and no transcript.
standouts: Concrete security critique of WebMCP consent semantics.
Runtime effect interception is a strong technical response.
advance_reason: Important and unusually creative WebMCP safety work with a clearly demonstrated attack-and-fix flow.

one_line: Semantic debugger that audits whether agent and human surfaces preserve the same intent and safety boundaries.
what_it_does: PARALLAX separates declared contracts from observed technical effects, producing traces, findings, recommendations, and PASS/WARN/FAIL parity results.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP provides the agent surface whose semantic effects are audited; structured traces and provenance expose failures that ordinary UI automation or HTTP success cannot reliably detect.
leverage_evidence: About text describes five page-defined meta-tools and a validated run_parity_audit invocation returning structured audit data.

execution_rationale: The BROKEN-to-FIXED audit narrative is coherent and the debugging UI is substantial, though broad adapter compatibility and automated remediation are not shown.
execution_evidence: Description gives a concrete simulated upgrade/charge semantic failure and read-only fixed path.
Video sheets consistently show semantic debugging, execution traces, and PASS/FAIL-style views.
impact_rationale: Developers building agentic websites have a real need to detect technically successful but semantically unsafe interactions.
impact_evidence: Problem statement distinguishes HTTP success from user-intent preservation.
Visible output is an explainable diagnostic trace rather than an opaque error.
creativity_rationale: Semantic parity as a first-class debugging target, with separate human/agent contracts and effect provenance, is a novel and ambitious developer-tool concept.
creativity_evidence: BROKEN/FIXED comparison makes semantic regression visible.
Product explicitly rejects surface equality as a sufficient correctness criterion.
usability_note: The trace-oriented UI is appropriate for developers but likely requires technical familiarity.
red_flags: Controlled playground is simulated rather than a broad external integration.
No transcript available.
standouts: Excellent semantic correctness framing.
Provenance-aware X-Ray traces and explicit fixed-vs-broken comparison.
advance_reason: Distinctive, technically meaningful WebMCP infrastructure with a clear developer audience and demonstrated diagnostic result.
